_about: Scheduler HINTS. Never acceptance gates. Raising a target changes WHERE the scheduler looks; it never changes WHAT is accepted. min_relevance, min_quality and accept_composite live in policy.v1.json, are read once per run, and are never touched by the scheduler. An unmet target is reported as an unmet target.
_overrides_about: Per-slug overrides, expected to be revised upward once real yield is observed. A slug whose coverage_policy is record_only may NOT be given a target above 0 — check_facets.py refuses it. That keeps decisions R4 (cross-industry never closes a concrete gap) and C6 (technology-software is never actively sought) enforceable in code rather than by convention.
_record_only_about: cross-industry, technology-software and other-unclear are record_only by decision. other-unclear is target_min 0 by construction: seeking more unclassifiable records is meaningless.

scheduler._stop_about: Any one of these stops the loop: max_rounds reached, newly accepted below no_progress_min, duplicate_rate above duplicate_rate_stop, global or lane budget exhausted, or all targets met.
scheduler._rank_about: Seven factors, not remaining gap alone. duplicate_rate and quality_rejection_rate are penalties: a lane that keeps returning duplicates or low-quality items ranks DOWN even when its gap is large. A gap lane opens only where a credible source exists; otherwise the round records stop_reason 'no_credible_source' and the gap is reported honestly.
scheduler._never_about: cross-industry never launches a gap-filling lane of its own and never closes or reduces a concrete industry gap (decision R4). other-unclear is meaningless to seek.
